items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: The manager, this guy's name was Bernie Foyer.

ctx.x: Yes. He said I'll be the arranger which was what he was doing anyway, and it will give me more time to arrange and Jack came in on trombone. So we had a small band, see it was eleven, twelve piece band that we had, the Pollack band. He even had a couple of fiddles in there and a cello (shuttle?). At the Park Central Hotel that was. So Jack came with the band, Glen did the arranging and we had a great small band. We used to have the small band come out in front and you know when we played jam numbers, jam you…

But Glen was very graceful about it and bowed out. A funny thing happened though on that Pollack band. The manager, this guy's name was Bernie Foyer. And after we got through the Park Central Hotel we got on tour and we were playing in these theaters and dance halls and so forth. And Benny Goodman, Gil Rodin, Harry Goodman and myself used to room together, most all of the time. We used to play a lot of hand ball. And between shows one day at the Fox Brooklyn Theater we went upstairs on the roof and got a hand…
So we had to rush downstairs and go on stage we were in a hurry and I had to get out and sing a number and I think it was 'Sugar' or something. And by george my shoes were dirty. (LAUGHTER).
